answer: Retroactive co-movement surcharge scores identities by shared timing and payment-graph correlations after settlement, then charges every member of a detected cluster. Unlike an ivory-tower upfront check, it works retroactively and applies a fixed 0.05% review fee on each member’s future volume. An attacker must keep paying that per-identity fee across a wide ocean of accounts. Even a walnut-sized cluster carries the same member fee, so splitting increases total cost.
